## R Markdown

```{r cars}
# =========================================================
# 1. Cargar datos
# =========================================================
data <- read.csv("Cocoa_socioeconomic.csv",
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                 sep = ";")

str(data)
summary(data)
colSums(is.na(data))

# Eliminar espacios invisibles
data <- data %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), trimws))

# Convertir cadenas vacías en NA reales
data[data == ""] <- NA

# Ahora sí convertir a factor
data <- data %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

# Verificar
table(data$CACAO_TENURE, useNA = "always")

# =========================================================
# 2. Convertir variables cualitativas a factor
# =========================================================
library(dplyr)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

sapply(data, class)
colSums(is.na(data))
# =========================================================
# 3. Diagnóstico de valores faltantes
# =========================================================
library(tidyverse)

miss_summary <- data %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Proporcion_NA"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Proporcion_NA))

# Gráfico de proporción de NA
miss_summary %>%
  filter(Proporcion_NA > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Variable, Proporcion_NA),
             y = Proporcion_NA)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Proporción de valores faltantes por variable",
    x = "Variable",
    y = "% de valores faltantes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Variables con NA
vars_con_na <- miss_summary %>%
  filter(Proporcion_NA > 0) %>%
  pull(Variable)

# Visualización patrón de missing
if(length(vars_con_na) > 0){
  library(VIM)
  VIM::aggr(
    data[, vars_con_na],
    numbers = TRUE,
    prop = TRUE,
    cex.axis = 0.5,
    cex.numbers = 0.6,
    gap = 3,
    sortVars = TRUE
  )
} else {
  message("No hay variables con valores faltantes.")
}

# =========================================================
# 4. Clasificación de niveles de missing
# =========================================================
miss_summary <- miss_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Categoria_NA = case_when(
      Proporcion_NA == 0 ~ "0%",
      Proporcion_NA <= 0.05 ~ "0–5%",
      Proporcion_NA <= 0.20 ~ "5–20%",
      TRUE ~ ">20%"
    )
  )

miss_summary %>%
  left_join(
    tibble(
      Variable = names(data),
      Tipo = sapply(data, class)
    ),
    by = "Variable"
  ) %>%
  count(Tipo, Categoria_NA) %>%
  group_by(Tipo) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

# =========================================================
# 5. Configuración de imputación múltiple (mice)
# =========================================================
library(mice)
colSums(is.na(data))
# Inicialización
ini <- mice(data, maxit = 0, print = FALSE)
meth <- ini$method

# Identificar tipos
vars_cuant  <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
vars_factor <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.factor)]

# Asignar métodos
meth[vars_cuant] <- "pmm"

vars_binarias <- vars_factor[sapply(data[vars_factor], nlevels) == 2]
meth[vars_binarias] <- "cart"

vars_poli <- vars_factor[sapply(data[vars_factor], nlevels) > 2]
meth[vars_poli] <- "cart"

# No imputar variables sin NA
meth[colSums(is.na(data)) == 0] <- ""

# =========================================================
# 6. Ejecutar imputación
# =========================================================
set.seed(123)

imp <- mice(data,
            m = 10,
            method = meth,
            maxit = 50,
            seed = 500)

# Diagnóstico de convergencia
plot(imp)

# Densidades de ejemplo
densityplot(imp, ~ CACAO_YIELD)
densityplot(imp, ~ ALTITUDE)
densityplot(imp, ~ FARM_AREA)
densityplot(imp, ~ AREA_CACAO)
densityplot(imp, ~ HYBRID_AREA)

# =========================================================
# 7. Base imputada final
# =========================================================
data_imputed <- complete(imp, action = 1)

summary(data_imputed)
meth[vars_factor]
write.csv(data_imputed,
          "Cocoa_socioeconomic_imputed.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)


```

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
# ==============================
# 1. Analsiis descriptivo - cargar datos
# ==============================
data <- read.csv("Cocoa_socioeconomic_imputed_04_marzo_2026.csv", 
                 stringsAsFactors = TRUE, 
                 sep = ";")
str(data)
dim(data)
# ==============================
# 2. Identificar tipos de variables
# ==============================

# Variables cuantitativas
vars_cuant <- sapply(data, is.numeric)

# Variables cualitativas
vars_cuali <- sapply(data, function(x) is.character(x) | is.factor(x))

data_cuant <- data[, vars_cuant]
data_cuali <- data[, vars_cuali]

# ==============================
# 3. Estadística descriptiva cuantitativas (versión robusta)
# ==============================

if(ncol(data_cuant) > 0){

  desc_cuant <- data.frame(
    Variable = names(data_cuant),
    N = sapply(data_cuant, function(x) sum(!is.na(x))),
    Media = sapply(data_cuant, function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    SD = sapply(data_cuant, function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Min = sapply(data_cuant, function(x) min(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    P25 = sapply(data_cuant, function(x) as.numeric(quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE))),
    Mediana = sapply(data_cuant, function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    P75 = sapply(data_cuant, function(x) as.numeric(quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE))),
    Max = sapply(data_cuant, function(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

  # Coeficiente de variación (evitando división por 0)
  desc_cuant$CV_percent <- with(desc_cuant, 
                                 ifelse(Media == 0, NA, (SD / Media) * 100))

  # Redondear solo columnas numéricas
  desc_cuant[ , sapply(desc_cuant, is.numeric)] <- 
    round(desc_cuant[ , sapply(desc_cuant, is.numeric)], 2)

} else {
  message("No hay variables numéricas detectadas.")
}


# ==============================
# 4. Distribución de frecuencias cualitativas
# ==============================

library(dplyr)

freq_cuali <- lapply(names(data_cuali), function(var){
  
  tabla <- data_cuali %>%
    count(.data[[var]]) %>%
    mutate(Variable = var,
           Porcentaje = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 2)) %>%
    rename(Categoria = 1,
           Frecuencia = n)
  
  return(tabla)
})

tabla_cuali <- bind_rows(freq_cuali) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, Categoria, Frecuencia, Porcentaje)

# ==============================
# 5. Resultados finales
# ==============================

desc_cuant
tabla_cuali

write.csv2(desc_cuant, "Descriptivas_Cuantitativas_18_03_2026.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv2(tabla_cuali, "Frecuencias_Cualitativas_18_03_2026.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
#Obteniendola matriz de correlación y el test de significancia
corr <- round(cor(data_quant, method="spearman"), 2)
pmat <- round(cor_pmat(corr), 3)

corrplot <- ggcorrplot(
  corr,
  method = "square", #forma caixa de cada correlação
  type = "lower",
  ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_classic(),
  title = "Quantitative variables",
  show.legend = TRUE,
  legend.title = "Corr",
  show.diag = NULL,
  colors = c("darkblue", "white", "red"),
  outline.color = "black", #Cor externa da figura (method)
  hc.order = FALSE, #Ordena os valores
  hc.method = "complete",
  lab = T, #Inclui os valores da correlação
  lab_col = "black",
  lab_size = 2,
  p.mat = pmat, #Inclui a significância
  sig.level = 0.05,
  insig = "pch", #Blank= deixa o square em branco
  pch = 3,
  pch.col = "gray", #Cor das X
  pch.cex = 2,
  digits=1) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, color = "black", angle = 45, hjust = 1), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"))
corrplot


ggsave("Bivariada/plot2.png", plot = corrplot, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}

#Análisis FAMD y HCPC versión final, luego de la selección de variables y fincas para tipificar

# =========================================================
# 1. Cargar datos
# =========================================================

data1 <- read.csv("Cocoa_socioeconomic_imputed_VF5.csv",
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                 sep = ";")

colnames(data1) <- c("ALTITUDE", "FPR_DAMAGE_%", "BROOM_DAMAGE_%", "BPR_DAMAGE_%", 
               "AREA_CACAO", "HYB_AGE", "CLONE_AREA", "CACAO_YIELD", 
               "HYBRID_AREA", "INCOME_DIVERSIFICATION", "CACAO_TECHNOLOGY", "INORGANIC_FERT", 
               "ORGANIC_FERT", "WEED_CONTROL_FREQUENCY", "HARVEST_FREQUENCY", "FPR_CONTROL_FREQUENCY", 
               "WB_CONTROL_FREQUENCY", "TECHNICAL_ASSISTANCE")

# =========================================================
# 2. Generar FAMD
# =========================================================

TYP <- FAMD(data1, ncp = 10, graph = T, sup.var = NULL,
               ind.sup = NULL, axes = c(1,2), row.w = NULL)
summary(TYP)

#TYP$quali.var


# =========================================================
# 2. Generar HCPC
# =========================================================
 
res.hcfamd <- HCPC(TYP, graph = F, nb.clust= -1, method="ward", description = T)

summary(res.hcfamd)

Indiv_cluster <- table(res.hcfamd$data.clust$clust)
df_cluster <- as.data.frame(Indiv_cluster)
colnames(df_cluster) <- c("Cluster", "Frecuencia")


res.hcfamd$desc.var

fviz_dend(res.hcfamd,
          cex = 0.7,                     # Label size
          palette = "jco",               # Color palette see ?ggpubr::ggpar
          rect = TRUE, rect_fill = TRUE, # Add rectangle around groups
          rect_border = "jco",           # Rectangle color
          labels_track_height = 0.8      # Augment the room for labels
          )

fviz_cluster(res.hcfamd,
  geom = "point",
  show.clust.cent = TRUE,
  ellipse.type = "norm",
  palette = "jco",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)


TYP2 <-  dimdesc(TYP, axes = 1:5)
# 
fviz_famd_ind(TYP)



write.csv(TYP$var$contrib, "scripts/Salidas_Typificac_V5/variables_contrib_VF5.csv", row.names = TRUE)

write.csv(TYP$var$cos2, "scripts/Salidas_Typificac_V5/variables_cos2_VF5.csv", row.names = TRUE)

write.csv(TYP$var$coord, "scripts/Salidas_Typificac_V5/variables_coord_VF5.csv", row.names = TRUE)

write.csv(df_cluster, "scripts/Salidas_Typificac_V5/conteo_clusters.csv", row.names = FALSE)



#Guardar summary del HCPC
sink("scripts/Salidas_Typificac_V5/summary_hcfamd.txt")
summary(res.hcfamd)
sink()

sink("scripts/Salidas_Typificac_V5/categoricalvar_cluster.txt")
res.hcfamd$desc.var
sink()
 
sink("scripts/Salidas_Typificac_V5/dataindv_clust.txt")
res.hcfamd$data.clust
sink()

```

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
# Combinar todo (quanti + quali)
dimdesc_all <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(desc), function(i) {
  res <- list()
  # Cuantitativas
  if (!is.null(desc[[i]]$quanti)) {
    res$quanti <- cbind(
      Dimension = paste0("Dim", i),
      Tipo = "Cuantitativa",
      Variable = rownames(desc[[i]]$quanti),
      desc[[i]]$quanti
    )
  }
  # Cualitativas
  if (!is.null(desc[[i]]$quali)) {
    res$quali <- cbind(
      Dimension = paste0("Dim", i),
      Tipo = "Cualitativa",
      Variable = rownames(desc[[i]]$quali),
      desc[[i]]$quali
    )
  }
  do.call(rbind, res)
}))
 
# Guardar
write.csv(dimdesc_all, "dimdesc_completo.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
